title: Credential split across lines by an unquoted shell line continuation
summary: A SendGrid-shaped key assigned in a shell script is broken after some character by an unquoted (or double-quoted) backslash and line feed, so the value continues on the next line.
rationale: The shell removes the backslash and the newline before tokenizing, so the assigned value is the intact key although the file bytes hold two fragments and a separator. The failure mode is a reader that sees only the first line (partial leak) or that rebuilds more than the language does. The mechanism is shell-specific: it does not extend to other carriers, to a carriage return before the line feed, or to single quotes (see the sibling Cases).

expectation.rationale: Flagged, with every fragment covered. POSIX and the GNU Bash manual (different maintainers) are both consistent with the reading that an unquoted backslash-newline is removed before tokenizing, so the value the program sees is the intact key. Stated as consistency of two texts, not as a provider rule; the key shape itself is the family's documented grammar. The separators (backslash, line feed) are outside the fragments. Synthetic, never issued: every value in the fixtures is built from the words SYNTHETIC and EXAMPLE, so none can authenticate.

sources.supports: If a newline follows the backslash, the shell shall interpret this as line continuation; the backslash and newline are removed before splitting the input into tokens.
If a backslash-newline pair appears and the backslash is not quoted, the pair is treated as a line continuation: removed from the input stream and effectively ignored.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
